sections.h2: Who bills Lee County property tax, and who sets the value?
sections.html:
Lee County runs property tax through two desks. The appraiser answers anything about worth, exemptions and where mail goes (239-533-6100), while the collector answers anything about paying (239-533-6000).

Sellers hit this split at closing. Neither office can do the other's job: the collector will not alter a value or exemption, and the appraiser takes no payments. Questions about a special assessment for roads, fire, water or sewer go to the authority that levied it, whose contact details sit on the tax bill itself.

  • Appraiser: parcel records, value, exemption files, mailing address.
  • Collector: bills, receipts, quarterly and partial plans, deferral.
  • Clerk: deed recording, stamp tax, and the petition filings for value disputes.

sections.h2: What are the Lee County tax deadlines, and does early payment pay off?
sections.html:
Real estate bills in Lee County open for payment on November 1 and must be settled by March 31 of the next year. April 1 turns any balance delinquent.

The state's early-pay scale starts at 4 percent off for November and shrinks by a point each month through February. A lender still printed on the notice after a payoff does not block the November discount, the collector says. March payments get nothing off.

Every Lee city shares this one calendar, from Cape Coral to Sanibel. Six ways to pay exist: web, phone, mail, in person, kiosks, and 24-hour lockers at four centers. Late tax needs more secure funds than a personal check or eCheck, so line up certified money before a closing.

sections.h2: What payment plans does the Lee County Tax Collector offer?
sections.html:
Three options exist: quarterly installments, partial payments and homestead deferral. The installment plan closes first.

Lee County Tax Collector plans, from the office's payment options page
PlanApplyKey rule
Quarterly installmentsBy April 30 of the tax year (applications open November 1)Estimated tax must exceed $100 per notice; payments due June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31
Partial paymentsNovember 1 to March 31Up to five payments per account; none online; no discounts
Homestead deferralBy March 31Age, income and lien rules apply; deferred tax becomes a lien and fire insurance is required

Discounts step down from 6 percent on installment one to 4.5 percent, then 3 percent, then nothing on the last. Skip the first payment past July 31 and the enrollment ends. Partial payments cover only the live tax year, never delinquent tax, and an owner already on installments cannot combine the two.

A sale midway through does not end the plan, since the incoming owner carries it to year end. Mention it to the closing agent early.

sections.h2: How do homestead and senior exemptions work in Lee County?
sections.html:
Homestead wipes out the first $25,000 of assessed value for every levy. A second slice, printed by the Lee appraiser as up to $26,411 for 2026, reaches only non-school levies on value over $50,000.

File Form DR-501 with the appraiser by March 1, online at leepa.org, by email to exemptions@leepa.org, by mail to PO Box 1546, Fort Myers, FL 33902, or in person at 2480 Thompson Street, 4th Floor, Fort Myers, on weekdays during business hours The office finishes processing by July 1. Save Our Homes, the cap on yearly assessment growth, starts the year after the grant.

Each Lee taxing body picks its own senior exemption amount for income-qualified owners aged 65 and over:

  • City of Sanibel, City of Bonita Springs and City of Fort Myers: $25,000.
  • City of Cape Coral: $50,000.
  • Town of Fort Myers Beach and Village of Estero: $50,000 and up to $250,000.
  • All Lee County millages: $50,000 and up to $250,000.

The appraiser also lists exemptions for disabled veterans, disabled first responders, surviving spouses, deployed service members, and $5,000 exemptions for widows, widowers, blind owners and others with disabilities. Most renew each January 1 unless ownership or residency changes.

sections.h2: What happens to a homestead exemption when you sell a Lee County house?
sections.html:
A buyer gets nothing automatically, so a new application is needed, and the seller's exemption drops off at the next turn of the year.

The appraiser warns that a TRIM notice showing homestead in the year of purchase reflects the seller's benefit, which will be removed. Sellers should also know that renting the property long term, or changing how title is held (certain trusts or LLCs), can end the exemption, and the office asks to be contacted when ownership changes in any manner.

If you move to another Florida home, homestead and the Save Our Homes portability benefit must be applied for again at the new address. Florida's state portability rule gives a three-year window counted from January 1 of the year the old homestead was given up, and the form is DR-501T filed by March 1.

sections.h2: How does a Lee County TRIM notice differ from the tax bill?
sections.html:
TRIM is the appraiser's mid-August preview. The bill, sent by the collector generally in November, is the real charge and the only one listing non-ad valorem items like garbage, fire or water.

The notice shows market value, exemptions, Save Our Homes status and proposed tax. A value dispute goes to the Value Adjustment Board within 25 days of the notice; a denied exemption has a separate 30 days from the denial letter. Keep both papers handy for buyers who ask about carrying costs.

On the Amendment 3 question, the collector's FAQ answers that it begins January 1, 2027 and leaves the 2026 bill alone. Millage differs by address across school, city and district levies, so rely on your parcel lookup and your own notice instead of any county average.

sections.h2: Who pays Lee County tax at a sale?
sections.html:
On the settlement statement the closing agent apportions the year between the two parties. The year's bill still goes to the owner of record when the roll reaches the collector, so a former owner may receive one.

Its advice: pass the bill to the new owner or the closing agent. A transfer is recorded with the clerk and then relayed to the appraiser, so lag is normal. Unpaid tax appears in the title search and is cleared from seller funds.

Lee County deeds carry the standard Florida stamp rate, 70 cents per $100 of consideration (Miami-Dade differs). Each party to the deed answers for it, and the clerk takes payment at recording.

sections.h2: Who lives in Lee County, and what are homes worth?
sections.html:
Lee County sits on the Gulf Coast and holds about 875,607 people by the Census Bureau's latest estimate, 15.1 percent more than in 2020, across 781 square miles.

Of 479,540 housing units, 74.3 percent are lived in by their owners, and for 2020 to 2024 the Census reports a $362,200 median home value and $76,107 in median household income. Residents 65 and over make up 29.2 percent of the population, which is one reason the senior exemptions above matter in sales. The county's municipalities named by the appraiser are Cape Coral, Fort Myers, Bonita Springs, Estero, Sanibel and Fort Myers Beach, and most owners outside those limits sit in unincorporated areas billed by the same offices.

faqs.q: Is Lee County property tax due every year on the same dates?
faqs.a: Yes, the calendar repeats yearly: open November 1, due March 31, delinquent April 1, with a shrinking discount from 4 percent in November to 1 percent in February.

faqs.q: Can I still join the Lee County installment plan after April 30?
faqs.a: No. The window runs November 1 to April 30, and a late applicant is left with the partial plan, open through March 31.

faqs.q: Does the buyer get my homestead exemption in Lee County?
faqs.a: No. Buyers apply themselves. A TRIM notice listing homestead right after a purchase shows the seller's old benefit, which is removed.

faqs.q: Whom should I contact if my Lee County value looks wrong?
faqs.a: Ring the appraiser at 239-533-6100. A formal petition on a DR-486 form is lodged with the clerk inside 25 days of the proposed-tax notice.

faqs.q: What happens if Lee County property tax is unpaid when I sell?
faqs.a: The title company clears it from seller funds, along with any added charges. Because personal checks and eChecks are refused for late tax, ask the collector which funds it takes.
